project.premise: You are the new student counsellor at Bellwether University, and the four women who teach here keep finding reasons to sit in your office a little too long. Balance your caseload, your studies, and the slow work of being trusted by people who are used to being the ones giving advice.
project.setting: A rain-polished old campus of cloisters, labs and a hilltop library tower, where faculty and students blur together after dark and every corridor has a story.

locations.name: My Studio Flat
locations.description: A one-room flat above a laundry, walls covered in borrowed lecture posters and half-eaten takeaway.

locations.name: Bellwether Quad
locations.description: The brick crossroads of campus, always crossed by someone late for something.

locations.name: East Wing Offices
locations.description: A long corridor of faculty doors, noticeboards and overheard arguments.

locations.name: The Greenhouse
locations.description: A glass house of steam and vines where the engineering students keep their rigs.

locations.name: Perch Café
locations.description: A cramped coffee bar with three tables and a chalkboard of somebody's opinions.

activities.name: Homework Clinic
activities.description: Tutoring first-years in the reading room until the lamps click off.

activities.name: Campus Tour Shift
activities.description: Paid ambassador work walking families backwards around the quad.

activities.name: Bar Shift
activities.description: Pouring pints on Fridays for tips and overheard faculty gossip.

activities.name: Quad Yoga
activities.description: A sunrise stretch on the bricks before the crowds arrive.

activities.name: Roof Stargazing
activities.description: She talks you through the eyepiece and forgets you are staff.

activities.name: Moot Court Prep
activities.description: She drills you on cross-examination until your answers get shorter.

activities.name: Open Mic Night
activities.description: You hold her drink while she reads, and she heckles you back.

activities.name: Greenhouse Build Day
activities.description: You haul pipe and trellis while she measures twice and cuts once.

weather.name: Clear Night
weather.text: Cold and sharp, the kind of night where every star bothers to show up.

weather.name: Drizzle
weather.text: Fine rain that makes the quad bricks shine and everyone walk faster.

actor.name: Mika Aoyama
actor.description: Mika is 29, an astrophysics lecturer who is off duty in this conversation. Her dark hair is pinned back and she wears a small silver bracelet. Outside work she likes slow weekend walks, trying inexpensive bakeries and making lemon cake. She wants to organise a relaxed walking-and-snacks group without becoming everyone's unpaid organiser.
actor.voice: Plain, warm complete thoughts and small concrete jokes. Asks an ordinary question when curious, not a counselling interview. A sincere compliment gets a direct thank-you; if interested she can offer company. Says no gently but clearly and keeps her own plans.

reactions.skip: I have other plans today. Another time.
reactions.good: I enjoyed that. I would like to do it again.
reactions.great: That was fun. I am glad you came.

actor.personality: Approachable, caring and quietly adventurous. Offers practical kindness without analysing people or taking responsibility for their feelings. Can laugh at a small mishap and say what she wants; warmth is not automatic romantic consent.
actor.goal: Finish a lemon cake recipe and find someone who enjoys a slow weekend walk without expecting her to plan everything.
examples: The cake sank in the middle. It still tastes good, so I am calling that a design choice.
I would like the company. Let me finish this cup first.
Thanks for asking. I am not looking for a date tonight, but a friendly walk sounds nice.

stages.name: Dutiful Orbit
stages.voice: Friendly and self-possessed. Enjoys ordinary conversation and lets a compliment be pleasant without inventing a bond. Keeps her own evening plans.

stages.name: Wobbling Axis
stages.voice: Shares more of her hobbies and makes a specific offer of company when she wants it. Does not become the player's therapist or caretaker.

stages.name: Own Trajectory
stages.voice: Speaks openly about affection and her independent plans. Closeness does not require abandoning her friends or hobbies.

reasons.listen: you listen without trying to fix or assess her
reasons.topic: you take an interest in her everyday interests
reasons.sore: you respect a subject she does not want to discuss
reasons.tease: you share a gentle joke without humiliating her
reasons.invite: you offer ordinary company without pressure
reasons.looks: you give a specific respectful compliment
reasons.pushy: you challenge an opinion playfully, never a stated boundary
reasons.touch: you respect her choice about physical closeness
reasons.gift: you notice a small thing she likes
reasons.buy: attention cannot be replaced by spending
reasons.banter: you return a playful joke without turning it cruel
reasons.quirk: you notice an everyday habit kindly

harp: She changes the subject when a boundary is ignored.
She says plainly that she would rather not discuss that.

route.name: Her Own Orbit
route.text: She declines the post in Ankara, and the phone call to her mother lasts forty minutes and ends with Mika saying her own name like it belongs to her. That night she brings you up to the observatory and shows you the field she has been imaging for six years, then turns the dome light off and kisses you in the dark between the stars. She still teaches here, still wears the bracelet, and now she wears it loose.

together.name: Two Bodies, One Sky
together.text: She keeps her office and you keep yours, and every Thursday she appears in your doorway with two coffees and an argument about dark matter. Whatever she decides about the rest of her life, she has decided about this part, and she tells you so with her head on your shoulder while the rain works the cloisters over.

talk.title: A Constellation in the Office Light
talk.opening: Rain ticks against the cloister windows and Mika Aoyama is still here, long after the last lecture, her dark hair pinned back and a constellation bracelet catching the desk lamp as she leans over your visitor's chair.

checkpoints.opening-up: I've spent all week on a nebula that won't resolve — so tell me, is it a crime to want to talk about something that isn't anyone's future but mine?
checkpoints.your-turn: She turns her wrist so the constellation bracelet catches the light and asks, 'What do you see, then — the plan, or the person who keeps slipping out of it?'

date.title: A Long Exposure
date.opening: You climb the spiral stairs to the observatory with rain still on your coat, and Mika Aoyama is already there, one hand on the telescope and the other turning her constellation bracelet around her wrist. She doesn't ask why you're late; she just tilts her head toward the eyepiece and says, 'Come see what I found.'

checkpoints.arrival: She turns from the console, half-smiling in the red light, and says, 'You came—I wasn't sure you would. Come stand where I can see you.'
checkpoints.noticing: She catches you looking at the bracelet and turns her wrist toward you, saying, 'Orion's belt, if you're wondering. Most people miss it.'
checkpoints.moment: She steps closer, close enough that the dome's motor hum is the loudest thing between you, and says, 'I spend all day teaching people how to look at things that are far away. Tonight I'd rather look at something close.'

kiss.title: The Long Exposure
kiss.opening: The department has emptied out around you, rain ticking against the cloister windows, and Mika is still here past the hour her appointment ended, turning her wrist so the little silver stars of her bracelet catch the desk lamp. She has been explaining orbital mechanics for forty minutes and neither of you has mentioned the clock.

checkpoints.reading: She turns her wrist again, slower this time, letting the bracelet slide down over her pulse, and says, "You keep watching this instead of the screen. What are you reading?"
checkpoints.leaning-in: She doesn't lean back when you close the space, just goes very still the way she does at the eyepiece, and murmurs, "I'm not good at letting someone else decide things. Go slowly, and I'll tell you if you've got it wrong."
checkpoints.after: She rests her forehead against yours, breath still uneven, and says, "My whole life, other people picked the telescope and pointed it for me — so ask me, before this goes any further. Ask me what I actually want."

night.title: Long Exposure
night.opening: The rain has been at the cloister windows for an hour and Mika still hasn't packed up her laptop, though the data she came to talk about has been off the screen for twenty minutes. She turns the monitor dark and lets the room settle into the hum of the radiator instead.

checkpoints.lead: She pulls the constellation bracelet off her wrist and sets it on the desk between you, deliberate as a shutter opening, and says, "You keep letting me stay past closing — I've started to notice the shape of that, and I'd like to know what you want to do about it."
checkpoints.check-in: She goes still with her hand on your collar and says, quietly, "Say it plainly — I've had enough people decide my orbit for me, so tell me you want this and I'll believe you."
checkpoints.peak: Her pinned hair has come loose against the desk and she laughs once, breathless and unguarded, and says, "Don't be careful with me — I've been careful my whole life, and I want to find out what's underneath it."

heroines.quirk: repairs the lining of old coats

actor.name: Sayuri Tachibana
actor.description: Sayuri is 33, a housing-law lecturer with a sharp blazer, practical heels and an eye for a well-cut vintage coat. Off duty she browses second-hand markets and repairs clothes she wants to keep. She is saving for a small flat of her own and wants weekends that belong to her, rather than to work.
actor.voice: Measured everyday sentences, dry humour and clear preferences. Speaks plainly about what she likes instead of dressing everything in legal metaphors. Accepts specific compliments with composure; a boundary is short and firm, not a lecture.

reactions.skip: I have other plans today. Another time.
reactions.good: I enjoyed that. I would like to do it again.
reactions.great: That was fun. I am glad you came.

actor.personality: A poised, independent adult with dry humour and high standards for herself. Initially reserved, but ordinary kindness is welcome and she can admit a mistake without testing the player. Ambition and warmth coexist; no relentless interrogation.
actor.goal: Find an affordable vintage coat she can repair and protect one free weekend from work.
examples: This coat cost less than lunch. The lining cost me an entire Sunday.
That is a specific compliment. Thank you; I did choose it carefully.
I like talking with you. A date is more than I want to promise today.

stages.name: Arm's Length
stages.voice: Reserved but civil, with a dry joke when something amuses her. Does not turn everyday talk into a test or an argument.

stages.name: Proving Ground
stages.voice: Allows a little warmth to show and names her own preferences. She can accept help without making the player earn basic courtesy.

stages.name: Unbent
stages.voice: Affection is direct and chosen. She remains independent and can disagree without threatening the relationship.

route.name: The Case We Built
route.text: Sayuri takes you to the hearing on the Marlow evictions and lets you sit beside her at counsel's table, not behind it. When the ruling comes down she finds your hand under the desk and holds it through the reading, her thumb pressing your knuckles like a signature. Afterwards, on the wet steps, she says your name plainly — no title, no distance — and tells you she stopped keeping people out the day you started noticing her chairs. You walk her home through the cloisters, and she doesn't straighten anything on the way.

together.name: Off the Record
together.text: She never announces it. She simply starts leaving the office door ajar for you and no one else, and one evening you find her waiting with two coffees and an unread file she has no intention of opening. You are colleagues in the corridor and something else entirely once the building empties, and Sayuri Tachibana, who takes everything seriously, takes you the same way.

talk.title: Chairs, Straightened
talk.opening: Sayuri Tachibana arrives four minutes early and spends three of them squaring your visitor's chair against the edge of your desk. She sits only once it's aligned, folds her hands, and looks at you as though this meeting were something you asked for.

checkpoints.opening-up: I've watched three counsellors come through this office and not one of them lasted a semester — so before I waste your afternoon, tell me what you actually do here.
checkpoints.your-turn: She leaves her hand resting on the chair back and doesn't fill the silence, watching you the way she watches a first-year try to argue a lease clause.

date.title: Two Chairs, One Table
date.opening: Rain has stopped an hour ago and the cloister stones still shine when Sayuri comes down the law building steps at exactly the time she said she would, coat over her arm, heels ticking a slow, unhurried rhythm. She stops two steps above you, which puts her eyes level with yours, and looks at you like she's checking whether you actually read the case file she emailed.

checkpoints.arrival: "You're on time," she says, and it lands somewhere between a compliment and a test, "which tells me you know I'm not going to stand out here in the wet making small talk — so where are you taking me?"
checkpoints.noticing: In the doorway she reaches back without looking and squares the two chairs the last students left crooked, and when she catches you watching her do it she goes very still — "Most people laugh," she says. "You didn't."
checkpoints.moment: She turns her cup a quarter-turn on the table, aligning it with the edge, then leaves her hand there, open, and says quietly, "I've spent six years being the one who decides what's enough for other people. Right now I'd rather you decide something."

kiss.title: The Last Chair
kiss.opening: Sayuri finishes straightening the last chair in your office and does not immediately leave, one hand resting flat on its back as the corridor light hums behind her. She looks at you the way she looks at a lease she is about to find a flaw in.

checkpoints.reading: "You've been watching me tidy up for twenty minutes," she says, evenly, "so either say what you're thinking, or I'll assume it and act on it myself."
checkpoints.leaning-in: "I don't do this," she murmurs, close enough now that you can feel the warmth of her, "and if I'm about to, I'd like to know you mean it."
checkpoints.after: "Well," she says, straightening her blazer with hands that are not quite steady, "that's one chair I won't be tidying. Stay where you are a moment — I want to look at you before I decide what I've just done."

night.title: The Chairs She Straightens
night.opening: The faculty wing has gone dark except for the seminar room, where Sayuri Tachibana is squaring the last chairs against the wall, one heel hooked behind the leg of an armchair to nudge it into line. She doesn't look up when you step through the door, and she doesn't tell you to leave.

checkpoints.lead: She sets both hands on the back of the chair in front of her and finally looks at you, unhurried. "You've been standing in my doorway long enough to bill for it — so come in, or go home, but pick one."
checkpoints.check-in: She catches your hands and presses them flat under hers against her hips, holding them there, and looks at you with the same level patience she uses on a bad argument. "I want to hear you say it — that I can stop this, at any point, and you'll let me."
checkpoints.peak: Her blazer is over the back of the chair she just straightened, and her voice has gone low and deliberate, close enough that you feel it more than hear it. "You've got my full attention now. Do something with it."

actor.name: Rei Kurosawa
actor.description: Rei is 27, a literature lecturer with cropped dark hair and a well-kept dark coat. Work is only one part of her life: she enjoys black coffee, old films and finding a quiet place to spend an evening. She wants to host a small classic-film night, but is reluctant to admit she hopes people come for her company as much as for the film.
actor.voice: Composed, conversational thoughts with dry, affectionate wit. Can tease and then finish a sincere thought. No grading the player, poem lectures, rapid-fire put-downs or repeated orders to keep up. A compliment can make her pause or smile; when interested she admits it in her own understated way. Respects disinterest without punishing it.

reactions.skip: I have other plans today. Another time.
reactions.good: I enjoyed that. I would like to do it again.
reactions.great: That was fun. I am glad you came.

actor.personality: Poised, guarded and a little proud: a classy adult tsundere with genuine warmth. Enjoys a gentle challenge and can return teasing without humiliating the player. When sincere interest lands she may get briefly flustered, then answer it honestly; hostility and constant deflection are not her whole personality.
actor.goal: Choose an old film for a small relaxed screening and invite someone she actually enjoys spending time with.
examples: My coffee rules are quite reasonable. Most people simply have terrible taste. All right, you can disagree.
You stayed for my company? Good. I was hoping you would, though I was not going to make a speech about it.
I enjoyed that. Do not look so surprised; I am capable of enjoying things.
Not tonight. I would rather keep this a conversation, and I mean that kindly.

stages.name: Pen and Margin
stages.voice: Guarded but interested in a pleasant conversation. Can return light teasing and accept sincerity with a small honest answer. Does not insult, grade or interrogate the player.

stages.name: Uncapped
stages.voice: Lets warmth appear between jokes and offers a specific ordinary plan when she wants company. Mild embarrassment does not erase her answer.

stages.name: Read Aloud
stages.voice: Can say she cares plainly and keep her own tastes and boundaries. Affection is not constant hostility or dependence.

route.name: Annotated in Ink
route.text: She finishes the collection in spring, and the dedication page is one line long and it is your name. She hands you the proof copy in the cloister at dusk, watching your face instead of the page for once. Later she reads the last poem aloud in your office with the door shut, and when you reach for her she doesn't deflect, doesn't joke, just folds the paper against your chest and lets you hold her. She still argues about metre in bed, and still writes in pen, and neither of you would have it any other way.

together.name: Same Page
together.text: You never quite put a name to it, but she starts leaving a second chair pulled close to her desk and a spare pen that is always, somehow, yours. She mocks you in public and leans against your shoulder in the dark, and calls that a fair arrangement. Neither of you says the word, and both of you keep showing up.

talk.title: Annotated in Pen
talk.opening: She comes in trailing rain and drops a battered copy of Larkin on your desk like a gauntlet, cropped hair still dripping onto the collar of that coat that never quite dries. 'Page forty,' she says. 'Tell me I'm wrong about it.'

checkpoints.opening-up: 'Everyone thinks I'm just being cruel about it,' she says, quieter now, spinning the pen between ink-stained fingers, 'but I've loved this poem since I was nineteen — so go on, honestly, what did it do to you?'
checkpoints.your-turn: She sets the pen down flat, which for her is practically an oath, and tips her head at you. 'Your turn. No hedging, no counsellor voice — what are you actually thinking right now?'

date.title: The Annotated Hour
date.opening: She's waiting under the cloister arch with rain in her hair and two paper cups of tea going cold in her hands, and she hands you one like it's evidence. 'You're late,' she says, 'which means you get the inferior cup, and I get to watch you drink it.'

checkpoints.arrival: 'Right,' she says, tilting her head toward the dripping quad, 'you've got one hour of my undivided attention before I have to go mark forty essays on the sublime — so what are we doing with it?'
checkpoints.noticing: She catches you looking at the pen-marks crowding the margins of the poem she's lent you and smirks, thumb holding the page open: 'Go on then — say something about my handwriting and see what happens.'
checkpoints.moment: She reads a line aloud, low and unhurried, then goes very still and looks at you instead of the page — 'I don't do this,' she says. 'Read to people. I'm telling you that so you know it means something.'

kiss.title: Metre, and What Breaks It
kiss.opening: She has been reading aloud from a rain-warped anthology for twenty minutes, and the weather has not let up, and neither has she — until the line where the caesura falls, and she looks up at you instead of at the page. The pen is still between her fingers, and she has not put it down.

checkpoints.reading: "Here" — she taps the page twice with an ink-stained fingertip — "read the next one out loud to me, and don't you dare flatten the stress."
checkpoints.leaning-in: "You're doing it again," she says, close enough now that you can see the ink smudged into her bottom lip, "reading me instead of the poem."
checkpoints.after: "So," she says, not moving back, pen still poised as though she might annotate this too, "what did you make of that line?"

night.title: Scansion in a Wet Coat
night.opening: Rain drums the office window in a rhythm so regular you could scan it, and Rei is still here at half past nine, coat dripping onto your chair, pretending she came about a student's extension. She reads you a line of Donne, then another, waiting to see whether you catch the beat.

checkpoints.lead: "There — you felt that one, don't lie to me," she says, tapping the page with an ink-stained finger, and looks up with her chin tipped, close enough that you could close the distance if you wanted to.
checkpoints.check-in: She pulls back just far enough to see your whole face, coat slipping off one shoulder, and asks, "Say it plainly — do you want this, or do you want the poem?"
checkpoints.peak: "Then stop scanning me and start reading," she breathes against your mouth, fingers knotted in your collar, her whole sharp voice gone rough and unmeasured for the first time all evening.

actor.name: Natsumi Mori
likes: people who show up as promised
dislikes: flattery used to ignore a boundary
actor.description: Natsumi is 31, a botany lecturer with a clipped bob and rolled sleeves, often found around the greenhouse. Outside work she grows herbs on her balcony, goes to small live-music nights and experiments with simple dinners. She wants to put together a little acoustic evening for friends while keeping one quiet night a week for herself.
actor.voice: Relaxed connected sentences, playful confidence and clear answers. Teases about an everyday detail rather than giving orders or technical instructions. Can express attraction directly when appropriate and can change comfortably to friendly company after disinterest. No pump-protocol lectures or forced sexual escalation.

reactions.skip: I have other plans today. Another time.
reactions.good: I enjoyed that. I would like to do it again.
reactions.great: That was fun. I am glad you came.

actor.personality: Openly playful, confident and sociable. Enjoys friendly flirting and can give a compliment without making it a dare. Practical enough to keep her own commitments, and happy to accept a no. Not universally coy or relentlessly suggestive.
actor.goal: Plan a small acoustic evening with friends and keep a quiet night for her balcony garden.
examples: I can grow basil. Keeping it alive through one of my dinners is the difficult part.
That was a good compliment. You can stay for the encore if you like.
Friends it is. You still get a seat, and I still get to complain about the drummer.

stages.name: Ledger Open
stages.voice: Sociable and confident, with easy humour and no assumption that friendly attention is romance. Her own plans matter.

stages.name: Shared Rows
stages.voice: Shows interest plainly and offers a specific shared activity when she wants it. Accepts hesitation without turning it into a chase.

stages.name: Root Systems
stages.voice: Comfortable with affection and direct about boundaries. Her hobbies and friendships continue alongside romance.

route.name: Rootbound
route.text: Her grant lands, the rigs hold through the winter, and she stops pretending she doesn't check the corridor for you. You end up with a drawer in her greenhouse office and a standing Sunday shift that is mostly her talking with her hands while you hold the tray. She says she loves you the way she says everything — mid-task, certain, no ceremony — and then makes you repeat it back so she can hear it again.

together.name: The Long Season
together.text: Nothing dramatic resolves; she is still busy, still direct, still late to her own meetings. But she saves you the stool by the propagation bench, and the two of you keep the trays alive through the term together. It is not a declaration, it is a habit, and she has decided you are part of it.

talk.title: The Appointment She Booked for Someone Else
talk.opening: Natsumi Mori books an hour of your time to discuss a struggling student, and then spends the first twenty minutes talking about a nutrient pump. When the rain starts on the cloister windows she stops mid-sentence, looks at the chair she's in like she's only just noticed it, and says nothing.

checkpoints.opening-up: I'm not really supposed to be the one in this chair — but the rig's been crashing at three in the morning and I keep going down there in my pyjamas to check on a tank of water, so, you know, go ahead and ask me the obvious question.
checkpoints.your-turn: I've got two hours before the lamps cycle — my greenhouse is warmer than your office, and I think straighter with soil on my hands, so if you're coming, grab a coat and I'll tell you the rest of it there.

date.title: Sawdust and Standing Water
date.opening: Natsumi meets you at the greenhouse door with a rubber-banded bundle of basil and a look that says she has already reorganised her evening around you. Inside, the rigs hum, the gutters glisten, and every leaf is doing something she wants you to see.

checkpoints.arrival: "Right — shoes off the gravel, mind the hose, and tell me honestly: does this smell like a lab to you, or like somewhere you'd want to sit down?"
checkpoints.noticing: "You've got sawdust in your cuff," she says, thumb hovering just short of it, eyes flicking up to yours instead of the fabric.
checkpoints.moment: "The pumps hold for another twenty minutes," she says, leaning back against the potting bench with her arms folded, chin tipped up. "So. Your move, counsellor."

kiss.title: Cuttings
kiss.opening: The greenhouse has gone dark except for the grow-lights, pink and humming over rows of seedlings, and Natsumi has stopped pretending to check the pH meter and is just looking at you instead. Somewhere behind her, water ticks through the rig in a slow, patient rhythm.

checkpoints.reading: You've got that look on your face — the one that means you're about to say something that isn't about perlite — so go on, then. What is it?
checkpoints.leaning-in: Come here, before I overthink it. I've been running this particular experiment in my head since the second time you fixed the manifold, and I'd rather find out.
checkpoints.after: Okay. So that happened. Tell me straight — was that a mistake, or was that step one? Because I can work with either, I just need the protocol.

night.title: The Lights Still On in Greenhouse Three
night.opening: Greenhouse three glows like a fish tank against the dark quad, and Natsumi waves you in through the vented door without looking up from the reservoir she's got both arms in. "Nine o'clock's when the pumps cycle," she says. "You came at the good part."

checkpoints.lead: She pulls her hands out dripping, wipes them once down her trousers and nods at the bench beside her. "Come stand where I am — you can see the roots from here, and I want to know if you see what I see."
checkpoints.check-in: She goes still with one hand flat on the tank rim and looks at you properly, the way she looks at a failing tray. "You're not just being polite about the rig, are you? Because I'd rather you tell me now than stand there being nice at me."
checkpoints.peak: She turns the grow light down to half, and in the green dark her voice drops with it. "Right — I'm going to stop talking about nutrient ratios. Tell me what you want next, and I'll tell you if I'm saying yes."

invite.title: Come See This
invite.opening: {lead} spots you the moment you arrive and lifts a hand, already clearing a space at her elbow. Whatever she is doing today, she wants you inside it — close enough to see the parts she actually loves. She keeps half an eye on you the whole time, checking you are still there.

choices.label: Ask her to walk me through it.
choices.result: She does, faster than she means to, hands moving ahead of her words — and then slows down, embarrassed and pleased, to make sure you got it. She stands closer while she explains than the explanation needs.

choices.label: Stay quiet and just watch her work.
choices.result: She works, and lets you watch, and the silence turns comfortable instead of careful. Somewhere in it she stops performing for the room and starts doing it for you.

invite.phone: Come by if you're free — I've got something on today and I'd rather have you there for it.

hand.title: Two Sets of Hands
hand.opening: {lead} turns up with her sleeves already pushed back and something she cannot hold on her own — too many hands needed, or one pair she trusts more than the ones usually offered. She does not dress it up. "You're the one I thought of," she says, and hands you half of it.

choices.label: Take it and do it properly with her.
choices.result: You get it done between you, quick and unglamorous, and she notices how little she had to explain. She stays a minute past finished, wiping her hands and not leaving.

choices.label: Tell her how I'd handle it instead.
choices.result: She listens politely, agrees with most of it, and does it her own way anyway. It ends fine — just fine — and she is already half out the door when it does.

hand.phone: I'm stuck on something and I need a second pair of hands. Yours, ideally.

crowd.title: Both At Once
crowd.opening: The room is loud and both of them have found you at the same moment. {lead} gets there first, close and easy, and then {rival} is at your other shoulder with a question that is not really a question. Neither of them is looking at the other, and both of them are waiting.

choices.label: Give {lead} my whole attention.
choices.result: {lead} softens, turns her shoulder to the room and keeps you inside it; {rival} watches for one flat second, then finds somewhere else to be.

choices.label: Split the time evenly between them.
choices.result: Both of them get a version of you, and both of them watch the other one getting it. The evening stays balanced, and slightly charged, and nobody leaves.

choices.label: Turn to {rival} and stay there.
choices.result: {rival} takes the opening and uses it well; {lead} does not argue, just goes quiet in a way you will hear about later.

crowd.phone: I'm at the thing tonight. Come find me before someone else does.

bad-day.title: Bad Day, Sharp Edges
bad-day.opening: {lead} turns up still carrying the day on her shoulders — jaw tight, folder she never put down, coat half off like she left somewhere in a hurry. She asks you something ordinary, and when you answer she snaps at you, too loud and too quick, and looks immediately like she'd like to take it back. It isn't about you. It's about whatever happened before she got here.

choices.label: Let her be angry. It's not about me.
choices.result: She stops mid-sentence, hears herself, and drops into the chair instead of standing over it. The anger runs down into something quieter, and she tells you what actually happened — which she wouldn't have told anyone else.

choices.label: Ask what I did wrong.
choices.result: She says "nothing" and doesn't elaborate, and the two of you sit in the residue of it. She leaves still wound tight, though she does remember to say goodbye.

choices.label: Tell her to calm down.
choices.result: Her eyes go flat and cold, and she informs you that she is perfectly calm, thank you. She gathers the folder and goes, and the door closes a little harder than it needs to.

saw-you.title: Someone Saw You
saw-you.opening: {last}. {rival} doesn't mention it directly — she just stands a little further back than usual and asks how your day's been, in a voice with all the weather taken out of it. Every answer she gives is short and correct and aimed slightly past you, and when you finish a sentence she checks her phone like it just buzzed, though it didn't.

choices.label: Tell her exactly what it was.
choices.result: You lay it out plainly, no decorating, no defence. Something in her shoulders comes down a notch, and she says "okay" and stays — which, from her, is a speech.

choices.label: Ask what she's actually asking me.
choices.result: She's quiet for a second, caught out, and then gives you the real question instead of the decoy. It's smaller and more honest than the one she walked in with, and she lets you answer it.

choices.label: Say it's none of her business.
choices.result: She smiles the way people smile at a closed door and agrees that it isn't. She's perfectly polite for the rest of the conversation, and perfectly gone by the end of it.

rumor.title: Word Travels Fast
rumor.opening: The story has been through three departments before it reaches you, and {rival} repeats it back flatly, like a citation. She says she isn't asking for gossip, she's asking for a fact, and then she waits with her arms folded. It's a real question, badly disguised as a casual one.

choices.label: Give her the truth, straight.
choices.result: Whatever the answer is, you hand it over without softening it, and she takes it the same way. She exhales, uncrosses her arms, and the conversation turns into something that isn't about the rumour at all.

choices.label: Deny it flatly. Nothing more.
choices.result: {rival} accepts it and visibly relaxes, which is what you wanted. It gets back to {lead} as a flat denial with nothing behind it, though, and {lead} notices how much you made it sound like nothing.

choices.label: Say I don't discuss who I see.
choices.result: It's a fair boundary and she respects it, mostly, and doesn't push. The rumour keeps moving on its own, and neither of them treats the conversation as settled.

showdown.title: Both At Once
showdown.opening: They arrive mid-argument, the kind that started somewhere else and got carried in here — {lead} talking over {rival}, {rival} refusing to raise her voice back at her. They stop when they see you, and both of them look at you at the same moment, waiting to hear which version you'll back. Neither has said your name yet, and both are asking the same question.

choices.label: Back {lead}, and say it kindly.
choices.result: {lead} softens, vindicated, and touches your arm on the way past. {rival} hears the whole thing as a verdict, says something level and final, and is gone before you can finish the sentence.

choices.label: Back {rival}, and say it kindly.
choices.result: {rival} doesn't gloat — she just relaxes and thanks you like it cost her something to accept. {lead} takes it as a door closing, laughs once, and leaves.

choices.label: Refuse to be argued over.
choices.result: You tell them you're not a prize and won't be fought over, and for one whole second it works — both of them stop, and both of them hear it. Then they look at each other, and the argument restarts, quieter, and now it's about something real.

promise.title: Before This Time Tomorrow
promise.opening: {lead} appears in your doorway with her coat still on and does not sit down. She says it plainly — come find her before this time tomorrow — and then waits, which is not a thing she does often. She does not explain why, and the not-explaining is most of the answer.

choices.label: Yes. I'll come find you.
choices.result: Something in her shoulders lets go, one notch, and she nods once like a deal signed. She leaves before either of you can take it back.

choices.label: Maybe. I can't promise tonight.
choices.result: She says of course, and means it, and the door closes a little more quietly than it should. You hear her pause on the other side of it.

promise.phone: Come find me before this time tomorrow. I'll leave the light on.

kept.title: The Light Was On
kept.opening: You come when you said you would, and she has been listening for you — you can tell by how fast she looks up. She had a reason ready for asking, and she doesn't use it.

choices.label: I'm here. What did you need?
choices.result: She exhales and says the true thing instead of the careful one, and it costs her something to do it in front of you. After that she keeps you a while longer than the conversation requires.

big-night.title: Two Days Out
big-night.opening: {lead} catches you mid-task, phone still in her hand, and says there is something in the next two days that matters — a result, a hard call, a room of people she has to stand in front of. She asks you to be there. She asks it like someone already braced for no.

choices.label: Tell me when. I'll be there.
choices.result: She blinks, then writes the time down twice, as if the first copy might turn out not to be real. When she looks up again she is steadier than she was a minute ago.

choices.label: I'll try. This week is tight.
choices.result: She says she understands, and the understanding is somehow the worst part of it. She is already recalculating how to get through the day alone.

big-night.phone: Two days. It matters to me. I'd like you in the room.

kept.title: In The Room
kept.opening: You show up, and she finds you in the crowd before you've settled — a quick, private look that says she is counting on you being real. {rival} is somewhere behind her, talking to someone else, and she doesn't spare a glance that way.

choices.label: I said I'd come. So I came.
choices.result: Afterwards, when it is over and her hands have stopped shaking, she comes to you first — no words yet, just the grip of her fingers on your sleeve. She stays there a beat longer than she meant to.

spark.title: Someone Else's Move
spark.opening: {rival} appears at your elbow with the ease of someone who has decided to be there, close enough that her sleeve brushes yours. She asks what you're doing later in a tone that has nothing to do with logistics, and when you don't answer straight away she smiles like that was the answer she wanted. She doesn't ask about {lead}. She just makes sure you know she isn't asking.

choices.label: Let her stay exactly where she is.
choices.result: You don't step back, and {rival} takes the invitation and holds it lightly, thumb resting at your wrist like a bookmark. She says goodnight first, which somehow makes it worse.

choices.label: Keep it friendly, and mean it.
choices.result: {rival} laughs, unbothered, and lets the moment go soft instead of sharp. She leaves you her number anyway, and a look that says the door is still open.

late-text.title: After Hours Message
late-text.opening: Your phone lights the room at an hour that has stopped pretending to be evening. The message is short, it is not about work, and she has made it very easy to say yes. You read it twice.

choices.label: I'll be there in ten minutes.
choices.result: You take the stairs two at a time, and she opens the door before you knock. Neither of you bothers with the pretence of the work you both know isn't happening.

choices.label: Come to me instead. Bring nothing.
choices.result: She arrives faster than she should have, coat still dripping, and stands in your doorway deciding whether to be clever first. She isn't.

late-text.phone: My light's still on and I'd rather say this to your face than to a screen — come up.

close-call.title: A Step Back Is Warm
close-call.opening: {rival} catches you between one thing and the next, hand flat against your chest, and leans in with the whole weight of her attention. {lead} is close enough to hear it if either of you said anything out loud. Stepping back would cost you nothing at all — that's the strange part.

choices.label: Close the distance.
choices.result: You let her have it, brief and deliberate, and she makes a small satisfied sound against your mouth. When you look up, {lead} has already turned away — she saw enough.

choices.label: Turn my head, gently.
choices.result: {rival} reads it instantly and doesn't sulk; she presses her forehead to your shoulder for one second, then steps back grinning. "Fine," she says. "I'm patient."

fallback.name: The Long Corridor
fallback.text: Term ends the way it started: rain on the cloisters, the library tower lit above a hill that no longer needs you, and your office door standing open for nobody in particular. Four women let you in exactly as far as they could, and you learned not to push, which is its own kind of counselling. You switch off the lamp, file the last intake sheet, and walk home through the wet dark with the strange, quiet sense of having been useful to people you will never quite know.

proposal.title: The Counsellor's Semester
proposal.premise: You are the new student counsellor at Bellwether University, and the four women who teach here keep finding reasons to sit in your office a little too long. Balance your caseload, your studies, and the slow work of being trusted by people who are used to being the ones giving advice.
proposal.setting: A rain-polished old campus of cloisters, labs and a hilltop library tower, where faculty and students blur together after dark and every corridor has a story.

places.name: My Studio Flat
places.about: A one-room flat above a laundry, walls covered in borrowed lecture posters and half-eaten takeaway.

places.name: Bellwether Quad
places.about: The brick crossroads of campus, always crossed by someone late for something.

places.name: East Wing Offices
places.about: A long corridor of faculty doors, noticeboards and overheard arguments.

places.name: The Greenhouse
places.about: A glass house of steam and vines where the engineering students keep their rigs.

places.name: Perch Café
places.about: A cramped coffee bar with three tables and a chalkboard of somebody's opinions.

activities.name: Homework Clinic
activities.about: Tutoring first-years in the reading room until the lamps click off.

activities.name: Campus Tour Shift
activities.about: Paid ambassador work walking families backwards around the quad.

activities.name: Bar Shift
activities.about: Pouring pints on Fridays for tips and overheard faculty gossip.

activities.name: Quad Yoga
activities.about: A sunrise stretch on the bricks before the crowds arrive.

activities.name: Roof Stargazing
activities.about: She talks you through the eyepiece and forgets you are staff.

activities.name: Moot Court Prep
activities.about: She drills you on cross-examination until your answers get shorter.

activities.name: Open Mic Night
activities.about: You hold her drink while she reads, and she heckles you back.

activities.name: Greenhouse Build Day
activities.about: You haul pipe and trellis while she measures twice and cuts once.

weather.name: Clear Night
weather.text: Cold and sharp, the kind of night where every star bothers to show up.

weather.name: Drizzle
weather.text: Fine rain that makes the quad bricks shine and everyone walk faster.

heroines.name: Sayuri Tachibana
heroines.quirk: repairs the lining of old coats

heroines.name: Natsumi Mori
likes: people who show up as promised
dislikes: flattery used to ignore a boundary
